record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: For exact cosmological solutions in heterotic M-theory and Horava-Witten cosmology with nontrivial Ramond fields, what is their full asymptotic significance, and what is the dimension of the asymptotic attractor formed by these solutions under perturbation of the basic regimes?

evidence.quote:
2.4 Asymptotics of M-theory cosmology
It is very important that there are some exact cosmological solutions in heterotic M-theory and Horava-Witten cosmology (with nontrivial Ramond ﬁelds) ... and so there are some basic regimes to perturb. An asymptotic analysis along the lines mentioned in this paper is expected to reveal for the ﬁrst time the full signiﬁcance of these solutions and especially the dimension of the asymptotic attractor they form.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider cosmological models arising from heterotic M-theory and Hořava–Witten cosmology compactified on the orbifold $S^1/\mathbb{Z}_2$, including their exact spatially homogeneous solutions in which the Ramond (form-field) sector is nontrivial. Regard these exact solutions as "basic regimes" inside the infinite-dimensional space of solutions to the corresponding equations of motion, and perturb them within the class of spatially homogeneous (in general anisotropic) cosmologies.

(a) Carry out an asymptotic analysis (toward the cosmological singularity and/or toward the far future) of these perturbations and determine the full asymptotic significance of the exact Ramond-field cosmological solutions: namely, identify which trajectories in the perturbed solution space are asymptotically attracted to these exact solutions, and characterize their stability properties.

(b) Compute the dimension of the asymptotic attractor formed in solution space by the orbits which asymptote to the family of exact Ramond-field cosmological solutions of heterotic M-theory / Hořava–Witten cosmology, i.e. the dimension (as a subset of the phase space of spatially homogeneous solutions) of the set of initial data whose evolution converges asymptotically to one of these exact solutions.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search returns work on exact cosmological solutions in heterotic M-theory and Hořava–Witten cosmology with nontrivial Ramond fields, and on asymptotic behavior of homogeneous braneworlds, but no source identifies the full asymptotic significance of these solutions or computes the dimension of the asymptotic attractor they form. The problem is posed as an open program and no definitive resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Cosmology and Heterotic M-Theory in Five-Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Five-dimensional heterotic M-theory with the domain wall vacuum solution provides the starting point for early universe cosmology in Horava-Witten theory.
status_evidence.claim: Exact cosmological solutions in heterotic M-theory exist and serve as background regimes.

status_evidence.title: Brane cosmology in the Horava-Witten heterotic M-Theory on S^1/Z_2
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of Horava-Witten heterotic M-Theory on S^1/Z_2 derive generalized Friedmann-like equations on each orbifold brane.
status_evidence.claim: Cosmological dynamics in this setting is studied but the dimension of the asymptotic attractor under Ramond-field perturbations is not determined.

status_evidence.title: Mixmaster Horava-Witten Cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: Form fields are dynamically negligible asymptotically but determine intermediate behaviour.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic role of form/Ramond fields is partially analyzed; full attractor dimension remains unresolved.
